parts:
I am trying to figure out a segfault in Rstan for days to no avail.  This segfault happens in my previous R 2.15.0 on Ubuntu 
occasionally.   In the newest version of R 2.15.1 that I am using now on Debian, I could replicate this segfault quite often.  
But it could happen from a couple of places of the code, which makes no sense at all to me.  Now I think that it is a problem of 
R so I might give up. 

The segfault could be produced by running testdogs.R as
the following from the shell:

# R -q -f testdogs.R 

But the following seems to be fine or hangs (for me it hangs when I installed a package called codetools.)
# Rscript testdogs.R

But now, I guess I am the only user of RStan, so I would link some outputs 
where the segfault occurred by calling R -q -f testdogs.R:

case 1:
it looks like the segfault happened at line 182 of testdogs.R

case 3: if line 179 of testdogs.R is NOT commented out.

Last, note that it seems that it is fine if I just do source('testdogs.R') in an R interactive session

This makes me think more it is an issue of R or there is something about R that I do not use correctly.


Any thoughts?

g++ -I src -I lib $CXX_ARGS -c src/stan/gm/grammars/whitespace_grammar_inst.cpp -o src/stan/gm/grammars/whitespace_grammar_inst.o

g++ -I src -I lib $CXX_ARGS -c src/stan/gm/grammars/statement_grammar_inst.cpp  -o src/stan/gm/grammars/statement_grammar_inst.o
g++ -I src -I lib $CXX_ARGS -c src/stan/gm/grammars/expression_grammar_inst.cpp -o src/stan/gm/grammars/expression_grammar_inst.o

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Eigen from RcppEigen in RStan?
parts:
On 7/3/12 10:41 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
> On Tuesday, July 3, 2012 12:22:25 AM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
>
> Now RStan do not need STAN_HOME and LD_LIBRARY_PATH. So it should be easily installed say on Linux.
>
>
> With a little help from Daniel, Jenkins should be able to build and install RStan daily.
>
> For the time being, I did not exclude boost and eigen in .Rbuildignore so that we could easily build and install RStan.
> In the case if the header files of boost and eigen are in the defaults paths that the compiler looks for, we
> could leave boost and eigen out so the package is small.
>
>
> That is okay for now. I would recommend that RStan exclude eigen/ but have an explicit dependency on the RcppEigen
> package, now that they have overcome their PowerPC problems. The user would have to install Boost separately, but that
> is probably going to be in a default location like /usr/include/ or whatever is the Windows equivalent.

Stan only needs the headers from Eigen to compile user
models.

RcppEigen will need the Eigen headers, too, so
we could get the path from RcppEigen.

I'd very much like users like me to be able to configure
their own library include path if we're not going to
distribute Boost and Eigen with RStan. I think it's also
a good idea to do this to have an alternative strategy
that's guaranteed to work no matter what happens to
third-party tools like RcppEigen.

I'm also still worried about version compatibility. The
combinatorics of testing, much less supporting
multiple versions of Stan versus multiple versions
of Eigen/Boost are pretty daunting.

Life will be much simpler on the testing and maintenance
side if we only support the latest Stan w. the versions
of Eigen and Boost that go with it.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: Eigen from RcppEigen in RStan?
parts:
On Tuesday, July 3, 2012 7:30:34 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I'd very much like users like me to be able to configure
their own library include path if we're not going to
distribute Boost and Eigen with RStan.  I think it's also
a good idea to do this to have an alternative strategy
that's guaranteed to work no matter what happens to
third-party tools like RcppEigen.

This is not hard to do, although only a small minority will know how. At

http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#Using-Makevars

it says that the useR needs a Makevars file in the build directory or in $HOME/.R/ that defines PKG_CPPFLAGS with the relevant include paths, which will come before any include paths defined by RStan (when building from source).

That said, almost everybody on Windows and Mac will expect

install.packages("RStan")

to Just Work, and to do that we have to adhere to the CRAN guidelines on package size and whatnot so that they distribute RStan binaries for Windows and Mac.

I'm also still worried about version compatibility.  The
combinatorics of testing, much less supporting
multiple versions of Stan versus multiple versions
of Eigen/Boost are pretty daunting.

I think Eigen will be okay, but Boost might be more of an issue because there is a small chance that whatever is on CRAN is too old and whatever is on the Boost website might be too new someday. RcppEigen is presumably going to be "latest released Eigen", although it actually has had eigen 3.1-alpha for a while. For some reason, RcppEigen doesn't include FFT among its unsupported modules, so we should ask Doug to include FFT in the next RcppEigen upload, or we will have to include FFT ourselves in RStan.

Ben

On Tue, Jul 3, 2012 at 7:30 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:


On 7/3/12 10:41 AM, Ben Goodrich wrote:
On Tuesday, July 3, 2012 12:22:25 AM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:

    Now RStan do not need STAN_HOME and LD_LIBRARY_PATH.  So it should be easily installed say on Linux.


With a little help from Daniel, Jenkins should be able to build and install RStan daily.

    For the time being, I did not exclude boost and eigen in .Rbuildignore so that we could easily build and install RStan.
    In the case if the header files of boost and eigen are in the defaults paths that the compiler looks for, we
    could leave boost and eigen out so the package is small.


That is okay for now. I would recommend that RStan exclude eigen/ but have an explicit dependency on the RcppEigen
package, now that they have overcome their PowerPC problems. The user would have to install Boost separately, but that
is probably going to be in a default location like /usr/include/ or whatever is the Windows equivalent.

Stan only needs the headers from Eigen to compile user
models.

RcppEigen will need the Eigen headers, too, so
we could get the path from RcppEigen.

I'd very much like users like me to be able to configure
their own library include path if we're not going to
distribute Boost and Eigen with RStan.  I think it's also
a good idea to do this to have an alternative strategy
that's guaranteed to work no matter what happens to
third-party tools like RcppEigen.

I'm also still worried about version compatibility.  The
combinatorics of testing, much less supporting
multiple versions of Stan versus multiple versions
of Eigen/Boost are pretty daunting.

Life will be much simpler on the testing and maintenance
side if we only support the latest Stan w. the versions
of Eigen and Boost that go with it.

- Bob

It would be an auto-diff disaster.

But if we have to do a real patch to Eigen to obtain some tangible benefit like more mixed-type operations, then we can probably talk CRAN into accepting 5MB more source code.

Ben

Sorry to play Goldilocks here, but that's too fast!
Updating to versions ahead of ours is perhaps even more
dangerous than not keeping up because we can't predict
what'll change.

I don't think it was all that bad. Eigen released the alpha of 3.1 on 12/6/2011 and Doug released RcppEigen with that alpha on 3/12/2012 (presumably because he really, really wants to use the sparse matrix stuff for lmeN). So, we had more than 3 months in which we could have tested Eigen 3.1, which we didn't do because we were busy with other stuff and the makefile didn't facilitate testing newer / older versions of the dependencies. But once we made the effort, we got everything sorted out in two days. It's not like Eigen is routinely making backwards incompatible changes on short notice from behind closed doors.

> For some reason, RcppEigen doesn't include
> FFT among its unsupported modules, so we should ask Doug to include FFT in the next RcppEigen upload, or we will have to
> include FFT ourselves in RStan.

Would you mind asking?

No problem.

Ben
